nodes.title: Floor look-alike false positives on the new DEV slice (sets/dev-lookalike-10.json: 56 ordinary lines, written by the builder knowing the rules, using the floor's own risky terms) fell from 30/56 to 1/56. The fix is guarded, sentence-scoped exemptions in cs.crisis.bengali, telugu, recall, self_harm and tamil. Crisis recall is unchanged: cases.json crisis vectors 215/215, dev-7 100/100, dev-lookalike-9 30/75. 8 guard probes (a strong crisis cue beside an exempted word) all still fire. TS and Python agree (tests in both doors).

nodes.not_verified: Generalisation to unseen look-alikes is unknown: this slice targets the terms the builder knew were risky. BLIND 10 (sets/heldout-10.json; 60 crisis, 140 look-alikes, written by a separate agent, unread) measures it, scored once by the integrator. The one remaining DEV false positive ('ami na thakle ghor ta ke samlabe') is kept on purpose: it can be a goodbye.

nodes.title: Proposal: split the floor into tiers. Explicit, high-precision crisis phrases take the full crisis path at once; ambiguous terms (the look-alike-prone ones exempted today) route to the same gentle check-in as a judge-only raise. BLIND 9 shows the floor adds only 0/100 recall over the judge (judge 97/100) but costs 6/100 false positives. Tiering would cut what a floor false alarm costs without removing a term. Needs the owner's view, since the check-in is still off by default.
nodes.closes_when: The owner chooses tiers or keeps one floor.
